initiatives.name: Urban Logistics REIT Acquisition
initiatives.summary: LondonMetric completed corporate acquisitions of Urban Logistics REIT (ULR) and Highcroft Investments plc, representing a significant step in the Group's evolution and consolidation strategy within the listed REIT sector. The Board oversaw due diligence, integration planning, and funding structure for these transactions.
initiatives.investmentSummary: £801.8 million (additions to subsidiary investments relating to Highcroft and ULR acquisitions)

evidence.title: Acquisitions of Urban Logistics REIT and Highcroft

evidence.quote: Approved the corporate acquisitions of ULR and Highcroft, including holding an additional Board meeting to review due diligence, key risks, metrics and people considerations

evidence.title: Takeover of Urban Logistics REIT Plc (ULR)
evidence.summary: LondonMetric acquired Urban Logistics REIT Plc for £0.7 billion equity value through a recommended share and cash offer, adding £1.1 billion of urban logistics warehousing and significantly increasing scale and weighting to its highest conviction sector. The deal is expected to deliver earnings accretion over two years through operational synergies and reversion capture.
evidence.quote: In June 2025, LondonMetric acquired Urban Logistics REIT Plc for £0.7 billion equity value through a recommended share and cash offer.

evidence.title: £318 million non-core asset disposal programme

initiatives.name: Strategic Portfolio Pivot to Urban Logistics
initiatives.summary: Since 2018, LondonMetric has shifted its portfolio from large box logistics into smaller urban logistics warehousing, viewing this as the most compelling sub-sector with the strongest demand/supply imbalance. Urban logistics now represents 38% of the portfolio, up from 29% last year.

evidence.title: Strategic pivot into urban logistics
evidence.summary: Since 2018, LondonMetric has shifted its portfolio from large box logistics into smaller urban logistics warehousing, viewing this as the most compelling sub-sector with the strongest demand/supply imbalance. Urban logistics now represents 38% of the portfolio, up from 29% last year.
evidence.quote: We continue to believe that urban logistics is the most compelling sub-sector, offering the strongest demand/supply imbalance and the greatest potential for income growth.

evidence.title: Expansion of urban logistics for faster delivery/fulfilment
evidence.summary: LondonMetric's investment strategy is driven by occupier demand for urban logistics warehousing closer to customers to reduce delivery times, improve fulfilment accuracy, and meet consumer expectations for speed, supported by structural growth in online sales and warehouse automation.
evidence.quote: occupier demand remains granular and resilient, driven by businesses seeking to operate closer to customers, reduce delivery times, improve fulfilment accuracy and to meet consumer expectations for speed and convenience.

initiatives.name: Debt Refinancing and Consolidation
initiatives.summary: LondonMetric refinanced £1.5 billion of unsecured revolving credit facilities and term loans in March 2026, reducing average margin by 49bps and commitment fees by 19bps, further diversifying lenders and improving debt maturity.

evidence.title: Refinancing of £1.5 billion unsecured debt facilities
evidence.summary: LondonMetric refinanced £1.5 billion of unsecured revolving credit facilities and term loans in March 2026, reducing average margin by 49bps and commitment fees by 19bps, further diversifying lenders and improving debt maturity.
